subject: LiveStream.ai pilot: first-token targets + chunking / fallback plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@livestream.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: LiveStream.ai pilot: first-token targets + chunking / fallback plan

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment ahead of the pilot kickoff: 

Recap of perf targets you confirmed on the call: 
- Desired time-to-first-token (first-token after request): <= 120ms p50, <= 250ms p95 for short prompts (<= 512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target for initial pilot: ~120 requests/min (burstable to 300/min)
- Concurrent user sessions expected: 40–80 active sockets during peak
- Streaming requirement: prefer server-sent events (SSE) for browser clients; websocket for mobile SDKs; chunk cadence ~200–400ms preferred for chat UI smoothness

Open technical items we need to validate (asks for your team):
1) Can you provide sample payload sizes and typical response lengths for the chat use case? (text only vs multimodal embeds)
2) Any strict region/data residency needs? (you mentioned US but wanted to confirm)
3) Are there any client-side limitations that would force us to choose a different chunk cadence (e.g., mobile CPU or bandwidth constraints)?

Proposed immediate next steps: 
- Elena: share a small set (3–5) representative requests and responses, and the sample traffic profile CSV by EOD Wed (I've attached our probe template).
- Aditya (cc): we’ll run a lightweight probe against our hosted cluster to validate p50/p95 numbers and capture first-byte/first-token timings.
- Logan: prepare a short playbook (fallback order: smaller quantized model -> regional fallback -> rate-limit advisory) and send by Friday.

Attachments: latency_probe_results.csv (probe template CSV)

Thanks — looking forward to the sample set.

Best,
Logan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai/docs/solutions
From: Elena Park <elena@livestream.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Brooks <t.brooks@edgecloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LiveStream.ai pilot: first-token targets + chunking / fallback plan

Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items below and answering your asks: 

1) Sample payloads: attached are three rows from our real traffic (summary only) — typical prompt sizes 80–300 tokens, response lengths 60–900 tokens (most under 300). We currently embed small transcript snippets, so payloads include ~1–3 small base64 blobs but nothing large.
2) Data residency: US only (no EU constraints for the pilot).
3) Client constraints: mobile SDKs will be on 4G in many cases; 200ms chunk cadence is ideal, 400ms is acceptable. We can't do extremely frequent tiny chunks (under 100ms) — it increases battery/network overhead.

Also FYI: Tom (EdgeCloud) asked that we validate behavior when a model fallback occurs mid-stream — we need a deterministic reconnection/fallback plan so the client can resume or show finalization without a confusing duplicate stream.

We’ll attach the sample traffic CSV by end of day tomorrow.

Elena Park
Head of Product, LiveStream.ai
elena@livestream.ai
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@livestream.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LiveStream.ai pilot: first-token targets + chunking / fallback plan

Elena — thanks for the fast reply and the clarity on cadence and residency. A couple of technical notes based on Aditya's initial probe and our internal playbook (sending for transparency, not final):

Summary of our lightweight probe (internal):
- Baseline cluster (gpt-medium quantized) observed p50 first-token = 95ms, p95 = 210ms for sample A (avg response 180 tokens).
- Under load (120 req/min, 60 concurrent steady), p95 slipped to 275ms — appears to correlate with small peak queuing at the batching layer; we can tighten this with aggressive concurrency limits and smaller batch sizes at cost of higher GPU utilization.

Proposed chunking & fallback policy for pilot (draft):
- Preferred streaming transport: SSE for browser sessions, WebSocket for mobile SDKs. Both expose a clear finalization event.
- Chunk cadence target: 200–350ms for typical chat responses; fallback to 400–600ms under degraded network to reduce overhead.
- Fallback ordering on service-side failure: 1) Retry same model instance (quick reconnect, idempotent stream resume token), 2) Switch to smaller quantized model variant (accept slightly degraded quality), 3) Regional fallback (if local capacity exhausted), 4) Controlled rate-limit message to client with ETA.
- Client behavior guidance: on reconnect, attempt stream-resume using resume-token; if no resume possible, client should request the rest of the message as a short non-streaming completion with a low-latency model.

Asks / decisions needed from LiveStream.ai: 
- Approve the fallback ordering (yes/no)
- Confirm that loss of per-token fidelity during quantized fallback is acceptable for pilot
- Confirm whether your client SDKs can support resume-token logic (we can add a shim if not)

I’m attaching a sample_chunking_policy.json that maps chunk cadence to response length tiers and fallback triggers. If you approve, we’ll lock the pilot SLOs as: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms (pilot baseline), with a follow-up run to see if we can consistently hit p95 <= 250ms after batch tuning.

Thanks — looping Jasmine to help with instrumentation and SDK guidance.

— Logan
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LiveStream.ai pilot: first-token targets + chunking / fallback plan

Short internal note — I ran an expanded probe last night against a more conservative batch-size config (lower max batch, lower batching window). Key takeaways: 

- p50 remained ~100ms; p95 improved to ~245ms at the 120 req/min steady profile.
- CPU jitter on our proxy nodes caused occasional 400ms spikes; Jasmine will instrument CPU throttling metrics and we’ll push a proxy hotfix early next week.
- I updated sample_chunking_policy.json with the rate-limit behavior and added resume-token TTL = 45s. Uploaded the updated file to the Drive link in the thread.

Action items I’ll take before the pilot kickoff: 
- Finalize probe runbook and share raw CSVs with Elena.
- Coordinate with Jasmine on the client resume-token shim and test across iOS/Android.
- Schedule a short alignment call with LiveStream for Wed 4/7 to confirm rollout.

-Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
